source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ θυσίαις πολλαῖς καὶ πλοκαῖς ἀνθῶν τιμῶμεν, οὓς ἄνθρωποι μορφώσαντες καὶ ἐν ναοῖς ἱδρύσαντες θεοὺς προσωνόμασαν, ἐπεὶ ἄψυχα καὶ νεκρὰ ταῦτα γινώσκομεν καὶ θεοῦ μορφὴν μὴ ἔχοντα (οὐ γὰρ τοιαύτην ἡγούμεθα τὸν θεὸν ἔχειν τὴν μορφήν, ἣν φασί τινες εἰς τιμὴν μεμιμῆσθαι), ἀλλ᾿ ἐκείνων τῶν φανέντων κακῶν δαιμόνων καὶ ὀνόματα καὶ σχήματα ἔχειν. Τί γὰρ δεῖ εἰδόσιν ὑμῖν λέγειν, ἃ τὴν ὕλην οἱ τεχνῖται διατιθέασι ξέοντες καὶ τέμνοντες καὶ χωνεύοντες καὶ τύπτοντες; Καὶ ἐξ ἀτίμων πολλάκις σκευῶν διὰ τέχνης τὸ σχῆμα μόνον ἀλλάξαντες καὶ μορφοποιήσαντες θεοὺς ἐπονομάζουσιν. Ὅπερ οὐ μόνον ἄλογον ἡγούμεθα, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐφ᾿ ὕβρει τοῦ θεοῦ γίνεσθαι, ὃς ἄῤῥητον δόξαν καὶ μορφὴν ἔχων ἐπὶ φθαρτοῖς καὶ δεομένοις θεραπείας πράγμασιν ἐπονομάζεται. Καὶ ὅτι οἱ τούτων τεχνῖται ἀσελγεῖς εἰσι καὶ πᾶσαν κακίαν, ἵνα μὴ καταριθμῶμεν, ἔχουσιν, ἀκριβῶς ἐπίστασθε· καὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν παιδίσκας συνεργαζομένας φθείρουσιν. Ὤ τῆς ἐμβροντησίας, ἀνθρώπους ἀκολάστους θεοὺς εἰς τὸ προσκυνεῖσθαι πλάσσειν λέγεσθαι καὶ μεταποιεῖν, καὶ τῶν ἱερῶν, ἔνθα ἀνατίθενται, φύλακας τοιούτους καθιστάναι, μὴ συνορῶντας ἀθέμιτον καὶ τὸ νοεῖν ἢ λέγειν ἀνθρώπους θεῶν εἶναι φύλακας.
pass_a_gloss: But neither with many sacrifices and braids of flowers do we honor those whom men having shaped and having placed in temples have named gods, since we know these things to be inanimate and dead and not having the form of God (for we do not consider God to have such a form as some say has been imitated in honor), but rather to have the names and shapes of those apparent evil demons. For what need is there for me to tell you things which you know, which craftsmen assign to the material, shaping and cutting and hollowing and beating? And from worthless things often, having changed only the shape through craft and having shaped, they name them gods. Which we consider not only irrational, but also to happen because of the hubris of God, who having unspeakable glory and form is named over perishable and needy things. And that the craftsmen of these things are licentious and have all wickedness, so that I may not enumerate, you know exactly; and they corrupt their own servant girls working together with them. Oh the shamelessness, that lawless men are said to fashion and transform into gods to be worshiped, and to establish such guards of the sacred things, where they are placed, not seeing that it is unlawful and to think or say that men are guards of gods.

pass_b_english: We do not honor with many sacrifices and braids of flowers those whom men have shaped and placed in temples, calling them gods, since we know these things to be inanimate and dead, lacking the form of God. We do not consider God to have such a form as some say has been imitated in his honor; rather, we consider them to bear the names and shapes of those apparent evil demons. For why should I tell you what you already know? You know exactly how craftsmen treat the material—shaping, cutting, hollowing, and beating it—and how, from often worthless things, they change only the shape through craft and fashion it, then name the results gods. We consider this not only irrational, but also an act of hubris against God, who possesses unspeakable glory and form, yet is named over perishable and needy things. You also know precisely that the craftsmen of these things are licentious and possess every wickedness, so that I need not enumerate it; they even corrupt their own servant girls who work alongside them. Oh, the shamelessness: lawless men are said to fashion and transform things into gods to be worshiped, and to appoint such men as guards of the sacred places where these idols are set up, not seeing that it is unlawful even to think or say that men are guards of gods.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the parenthetical remark regarding the form of God and the description of the craftsmen's actions. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.

reasons: Pass A omits the clause 'ἐπεὶ ἄψυχα καὶ νεκρὰ ταῦτα γινώσκομεν καὶ θεοῦ μορφὴν μὴ ἔχοντα (οὐ γὰρ τοιαύτην ἡγούμεθα τὸν θεὸν ἔχειν τὴν μορφήν, ἣν φασὶ τινες εἰς τιμὴν μεμιμῆσθαι)' which is a key part of the argument in the source text.

Pass A incorrectly renders 'ἐπὶ φθαρτοῖς καὶ δεομένοις θεραπείας πράγμασιν' as 'over perishable and needy things' instead of 'over perishable and needing healing things', which alters the meaning of the original Greek.

Pass A fails to preserve the full meaning of 'ὄνομα καὶ σχῆμα ἔχειν' as 'have the names and shapes' instead of 'have names and shapes', which is a minor but significant deviation from the original Greek.
